definition_short: After 75 moves by each player with no capture and no pawn move, the game is drawn automatically.
definition_long:
FIDE Art. 9.6.2: the game is drawn if 'any series of at least 75 moves have been made by each player without the movement of any pawn and without any capture. If the last move resulted in checkmate, that shall take precedence.'

The automatic counterpart to the claimable fifty-move rule. The checkmate proviso is the interesting part: a move that simultaneously completes the 75 and delivers mate is a win, not a draw.

preconditions: 150 ply have elapsed with no capture and no pawn move
indicators_against: The final move delivers checkmate — mate takes precedence
recognition.detector: lib/matchers.js: seventy-five-move-rule, over the halfmove clock

exceptions: Checkmate on the 75th move takes precedence over the draw.
limitations: Reported from 130 ply. Unlike the fifty-move rule this needs no claim, which is the difference the wording carries.

TYPICAL_CONFIDENCE RAISED medium -> high, 2026-09-02, and the reason is the schema's own definition of the field: 'how confidently this concept can normally be asserted ONCE ITS PRECONDITIONS HOLD'. This concept's recognition is MECHANICAL and its knowledge type already carries a high ceiling, so once the preconditions hold there is nothing left to be uncertain about - a stalemate is a stalemate, and a fork this base reports is one findMotifs() found, which ARCHITECTURE.md makes the authority and forbids second-guessing. 'Medium' was the default across 32 rule and motif records regardless of detectability, and it was found by measuring what the API reports against what each record permits: twelve concepts were reporting ABOVE their own record. The fix was to make each record its own ceiling in cap(), which then required the records that were wrong to be corrected rather than silently overruled.

examples.note: Constructed to sit one ply short of the rule. The halfmove clock reads 149; the rule is 75 moves by each player without a capture or a pawn move, which is 150 halfmoves, and it is the ARBITER'S rule rather than a claim: unlike the fifty-move rule nobody has to invoke it, the game is drawn automatically. The material is deliberately a rook ending White wins with correct play - the rule does not care, and that is what distinguishes it from `dead-position` and from `insufficient-material`.

by_level.beginner: Seventy-five moves have passed for each side with no capture and no pawn move, so the game is automatically drawn.
by_level.intermediate: The seventy-five-move rule ends the game without a claim — unless the last move was checkmate.
by_level.advanced: Art. 9.6.2, including the checkmate precedence clause.
